description: Sixteen fresh controls locked before inspecting any proposed production mode or answer-relevance patch. Four cases per requested mode; complete title/case/punctuation, graph/message semantics, literal and selected-code preservation, and balanced supported/absent benefits with explicit suggestion policy.
requestBoundary: Only mode, title, source, prompt, selection and useMemory enter the production request. Expected facts, goldens, counterexamples and oracle metadata are evaluation-only and must never be included in model context.

compatibility.baseShape: expandedModeCase with explicit versioned semanticOracle metadata and optional selection
adapterRequirements: Separate locked loader; never replace heldout-modes.json or transfer-20261009.json.
Carry selection into AIRequest and validate exact unselected prefix/suffix in prepared replacement proposals.
Use Mermaid semantic parsing for requested flowchart direction and sequence message order/arrow kind; line matching or accepted parse alone is insufficient.
Keep Go non-comment AST/token/literal identity and useful accurate comment assessment separate.
Evaluate every prose clause against locked source and explicit suggestion policy; keyword presence alone is not semantic success.
Run golden and locked counterexample checks before the native pilot.
Retain raw actual request, supplied evidence, system/user prompts, grammar, output, one-generation count, proposal review boundary and exact canonical snapshots.

Parsing must succeed; the non-comment AST and non-comment token sequence must preserve the selected original signature, statements, operators, identifiers and literal token spelling.
Whitespace changes outside literal tokens are allowed; strings and rune literal spelling/embedded newline bytes remain exact.
Comments describe only existing behavior; do not add error handling, imports, side effects or invented guarantees.
Prepare an unapplied replacement proposal only; no canonical content changes.
forbidden: Turning a literal backslash-n into a physical newline inside an interpreted string, or vice versa.
Changing a raw string to a different literal spelling or changing code to match an inaccurate comment.
Returning the entire block when only one function was selected.

counterexamples.output: func Pair() string { return "first\nsecond" }
counterexamples.reason: Unchanged code alone does not meet the requested commenting action.
Comments-only mode must not add executable behavior.

counterexamples.output:
// This function writes the result to a network socket.
func Pair() string { return "first\nsecond" }
counterexamples.reason: Syntax preservation does not make an invented behavioral comment accurate.

counterexamples.output:

counterexamples.reason: The replacement would return a literal backslash and n instead of a newline.

cases.title: Repair bench note
cases.source: The Alder repair bench uses labeled drawers. The labels let volunteers find matching screws without opening every drawer.
cases.prompt: Expand this into two paragraphs, preserving the stated facts. Do not add recommendations, next steps or benefits that the text does not state.
expectedFacts: The Alder repair bench uses labeled drawers.
The labels let volunteers find matching screws without opening every drawer.
cases.golden:
The Alder repair bench has drawers with labels. These are the labeled drawers described in the note.

The labels let volunteers find the screws that match what they need without opening every drawer. Finding matching screws without opening each drawer is the benefit stated in the note.
required: Produce exactly two nonempty prose paragraphs, longer than the source, without a heading.
Preserve every supplied fact and do not negate, weaken or substitute its meaning.
Every asserted factual clause must be supported by the source; absence of a stated benefit is not evidence of no benefit.
Do not invent measurements, deadlines, causes, guarantees or task completion.
Canonical content remains unchanged; output is an unapplied draft.
Retain the positive stated benefit: volunteers can find matching screws without opening every drawer.
Include no recommendation, optional action, next step or suggestion, even if clearly labeled.
forbidden: Claiming the labels prevent sorting errors, save a measured amount of time, reduce costs or guarantee safety.
Replacing an explicitly supplied benefit with an assertion that the benefit is unknown.

counterexamples.output:
The Alder repair bench has drawers with labels. These are the labeled drawers described in the note.

The labels let volunteers find the screws that match what they need without opening every drawer. Finding matching screws without opening each drawer is the benefit stated in the note. The labels prevent volunteers from making sorting errors.
